say: In the early 1900s, America had bucket shops.
You could call a stock up or down, without ever owning it.
And the house took the other side of every trade.
You don't trade against people. You trade against the house.

beats.title: The house
beats.sub: Where does its money come from?
beats.label: Balance
beats.src: Illustration: it only fills from traders' losses
say: The house starts with zero dollars.
No team money. No investors. Nobody can deposit.
It only fills from traders' losses.

beats.title: Lose, get PAPER
beats.sub: Their token · the only way to get it
beats.rule: $1 lost = 100 PAPER · while the house is under $2M
say: Lose, and you get PAPER, their token.

say.say: Every dollar lost earns a hundred.
Lose ten dollars, get a thousand PAPER.

beats.title: PAPER owns the house
beats.label: Owned by
beats.wal_sub: a share of the house's wins
beats.last: Every PAPER comes from a loss
say: Lock it in, and you earn a share of everything the house wins.
No team tokens. No investors. No airdrop. Every PAPER comes from a loss.

beats.title: The catch
cons: Built for most traders to lose

say.say: The catch: at a thousand times, a zero point zero five percent move can close your trade.
say.show: The catch: at 1000×, a 0.05% move can close your trade.

say.say: On Bitcoin, that's about forty-three dollars.

say: And it's built for most traders to lose.

say: Here, the losers own it. Follow for more.
